subject.title: [Feature]: Automatic Output Sanitization for Sensitive Data

question: Should OpenClaw add automatic final-output sensitive-value sanitization as a core security/config feature, route it to a plugin using outbound hooks, or keep core limited to the current log/tool/transcript redaction boundaries?
rationale: The requested behavior changes what users and models see, adds a new config/security boundary, and can create false positives or missed-surface leaks; source inspection shows the implementation gap but not the intended product boundary.

options.title: Define a narrow core security feature
options.body: Approve a maintainer/security design for opt-in or explicitly scoped core output sanitization with schema/docs/tests and no duplicate redaction engine.

options.title: Route to plugin or ClawHub
options.body: Use reply_payload_sending/message_sending hooks for an optional sanitizer plugin if maintainers want to keep core delivery policy lean.

options.title: Close or narrow to existing redaction
options.body: Declare logs, transcripts, tool payloads, and diagnostics as the supported core redaction boundary and close or split any remaining requests.

recommendation.title: Define a narrow core security feature
recommendation.body: Approve a maintainer/security design for opt-in or explicitly scoped core output sanitization with schema/docs/tests and no duplicate redaction engine.

likelyOwner.reason: This owner group is the CODEOWNERS route for secrets/security-sensitive config and should decide the security boundary before implementation.
